title: Laws, rules, principles, effects, paradoxes, limits, constants, experiments, thought-experiments in physics
summary: This is a compact reference glossary of named concepts in physics, arranged alphabetically from Ampere's law through to the Zeeman effect. Each entry gives a short plain-language statement of a law, principle, effect, paradox, limit, constant or experiment, often with the name of its discoverer and a date. The entries range across classical mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, quantum theory, relativity and cosmology. Among the items covered are Avogadro's hypothesis, Bode's law, the Chandrasekhar limit, Coulomb's law, the Davisson-Germer experiment, the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen effect, Hawking radiation, the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, Hubble's law, Maxwell's demon, the grandfather paradox and the laws of thermodynamics. Many entries include a worked illustration or a brief explanation of why the idea matters, and some discuss later revisions of older theories or common misunderstandings. The work is intended as a study aid and quick-reference guide for students and general readers. It circulated as a plain-text file on an early electronic bulletin-board network, and its wording is informal with occasional typographical errors.
